adds.title: LGBTQ people in prison - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Thin for Belize: the article (fetched, HTTP 200) surveys how LGBTQ prisoners worldwide are affected by strip-searching, solitary confinement, a disproportionate-incarceration risk, and transgender placement debates (including the US context), but its only Belize mention is a 'Violence in Belize' navbox taxonomy link. It contains no Belize-specific practice: no birth-sex-vs-identity housing rule, no trans special units, and no solitary/segregation practice for trans prisoners in Belize; no usable placement finding.

records.note: No Belize prison-housing placement data for trans prisoners was found: the mandated enwiki full-text search returned the generic 'LGBTQ people in prison' as top hit, and the fetched article confirms no Belize-specific placement content (only a navbox listing). No known-good org source (PRI/HRW/ILGA World or national orgs) documents how trans prisoners are housed in Belize - Belize has no legal gender recognition and a small prison system, and the only notable court ruling, the 2016 Orozco v AG decriminalisation, addresses same-sex conduct, not custody placement; no usable finding.

adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Haiti - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Thin for the prison-housing axis: the fetched article (HTTP 200) documents Haiti's legal framework - same-sex conduct legal since 1791, no legal gender-identity recognition, no anti-discrimination protections, and a June 2017 Senate bill penalising same-sex marriage with up to three years' imprisonment - plus documented harassment of transgender people in post-earthquake camps. It contains no prison-placement practice: no birth-sex-vs-identity housing rule, no trans special units, and no solitary/segregation practice for trans prisoners; no usable placement finding.

records.note: No Haitian prison-housing placement data for trans prisoners was found: the mandated enwiki full-text search surfaced 'LGBTQ rights in Haiti' (the only Haiti-specific candidate), and the fetched article confirms the only prison-related content is the 2017 Senate gay-marriage bill (up to 3 years), not custody placement. With the state apparatus largely collapsed and no functioning judiciary (base-lane sources) and no legal gender recognition, no citable source documents where trans prisoners are housed - no birth-sex-vs-identity rule, no special units, no solitary/segregation practice; no usable finding.
